```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, fig.align = "center",
  warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, dev = "png", dpi = 150
)
```

```{r load}
library(censusindia)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

data("census_2001_pca")
data("census_2001_pca_full")
data("census_2011_pca")
```

```{r design}
col <- census_colors()
theme_set(theme_census())

SRC <- "Source: Census of India, Primary Census Abstract"
```

```{r rounds}
bind_rows(
  census_2001_pca |> mutate(round = "2001"),
  census_2011_pca |> mutate(round = "2011")
) |>
  group_by(round) |>
  summarise(
    districts = n(),
    population = sum(population),
    literate_pct = share(sum(literate), sum(population)),
    worker_pct = share(sum(workers), sum(population)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(population = format(population, big.mark = ",")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

```{r geometry}
geo_2001 <- census_2001_pca |>
  mutate(literate_pct = share(literate, population)) |>
  attach_geometry(2001, geography = "district")

geo_2011 <- census_2011_pca |>
  mutate(literate_pct = share(literate, population)) |>
  attach_geometry(2011, geography = "district")

c(`2001` = nrow(geo_2001), `2011` = nrow(geo_2011))
```

```{r literacy-maps, fig.height = 5.5, fig.width = 10}
compare_maps(
  list("2001" = geo_2001, "2011" = geo_2011), "literate_pct",
  palette = "blue_red", reverse = TRUE, midpoint = 55, limits = c(30, 80),
  oob = scales::squish, na_color = "grey85", legend_title = "Literate (%)",
  show_state_boundaries = FALSE
) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Literacy rises from 54.5% to 63.1% of the population",
    subtitle = "Each round on its own district boundaries. Grey = unmatched",
    caption = SRC,
    theme = theme_census()
  )
```

```{r state-change, fig.height = 8}
states <- bind_rows(
  y2001 = get_census(2001, "state", variables = "literacy_rate"),
  y2011 = get_census(2011, "state", variables = "literacy_rate"),
  .id = "round"
) |>
  select(state_name_harmonized, round, literacy_rate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = round, values_from = literacy_rate) |>
  filter(!is.na(y2001), !is.na(y2011)) |>
  mutate(
    gain = y2011 - y2001,
    state_name_harmonized = reorder(state_name_harmonized, y2011)
  )

ggplot(states, aes(y = state_name_harmonized)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = y2001, xend = y2011, yend = state_name_harmonized),
    colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(x = y2001), colour = "grey55", size = 2.4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = y2011), colour = col[["accent"]], size = 2.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Literate, % of population", y = NULL,
    title = "Every state gains literacy between 2001 and 2011",
    subtitle = "Grey point = 2001, blue point = 2011. Ordered by 2011 level",
    caption = SRC
  )
```

```{r full-shape}
c(
  columns_shared = ncol(census_2001_pca),
  columns_full = ncol(census_2001_pca_full),
  rows_full = nrow(census_2001_pca_full),
  sectors = dplyr::n_distinct(census_2001_pca_full$sector)
)
```

```{r rural-urban, fig.height = 5}
census_2001_pca_full |>
  filter(sector != "total") |>
  group_by(sector) |>
  summarise(
    literate = share(sum(literate), sum(population)),
    workers = share(sum(workers), sum(population)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-sector) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, name, fill = sector)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(rural = "#999999", urban = col[["accent"]]), name = NULL) +
  labs(
    x = "% of population", y = NULL,
    title = "Urban India is more literate but no more likely to be working, 2001",
    caption = SRC
  )
```

```{r worker-categories, fig.height = 5}
census_2001_pca_full |>
  filter(sector == "total") |>
  summarise(
    Cultivators = sum(main_cultivators),
    `Agricultural labourers` = sum(main_agri_labour),
    `Household industry` = sum(main_hh_industry),
    `Other work` = sum(main_other)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "category", values_to = "workers") |>
  ggplot(aes(workers / 1e6, reorder(category, workers))) +
  geom_col(fill = col[["accent"]], width = 0.65) +
  labs(
    x = "Main workers (millions)", y = NULL,
    title = "Cultivation and agricultural labour account for half of main workers, 2001",
    subtitle = "Only census_2001_pca_full carries the category breakdown",
    caption = SRC
  )
```

```{r literacy-gap, fig.height = 8}
census_2001_pca_full |>
  filter(sector == "total") |>
  group_by(state_name_harmonized) |>
  summarise(
    male = share(sum(literate_male), sum(males)),
    female = share(sum(literate_female), sum(females)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(gap = male - female, state_name_harmonized = reorder(state_name_harmonized, gap)) |>
  ggplot(aes(gap, state_name_harmonized, fill = gap)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = col[["mid"]], high = col[["high"]], guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Male minus female literacy (percentage points)", y = NULL,
    title = "The literacy gender gap is 18 points nationally in 2001",
    subtitle = "Sex splits come from census_2001_pca_full",
    caption = SRC
  )
```

```{r claims, include = FALSE}
# Titles above state specific numbers. Fail the build rather than ship a stale one.
f <- dplyr::filter(census_2001_pca_full, sector == "total")
stopifnot(
  nrow(census_2001_pca) == 593, nrow(census_2011_pca) == 640,
  round(share(sum(census_2001_pca$literate), sum(census_2001_pca$population)), 1) == 54.5,
  round(share(sum(census_2011_pca$literate), sum(census_2011_pca$population)), 1) == 63.1,
  all(states$gain > 0),
  round(share(sum(f$literate_male), sum(f$males)) -
    share(sum(f$literate_female), sum(f$females))) == 18,
  sum(f$main_cultivators) + sum(f$main_agri_labour) >
    sum(f$main_hh_industry) + sum(f$main_other)
)
```
